subject: Web Development
subcategory: Famous Websites That Changed the World
title: Facebook: The Real-Name Network
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Facebook: The Real-Name Network.

hook.text: In 2004, Mark Zuckerberg launched Facebook from a Harvard dorm room. It required a .edu email.

buildup.text: Unlike MySpace, Facebook used real names and real identities. Authenticity was the feature.

discovery.text: The News Feed, launched in 2006, turned the web into a real-time stream of friends' updates.

twist.text: Facebook's data practices led to the Cambridge Analytica scandal, shaking public trust.

climax.text: With three billion users, Facebook reshaped how humanity communicates and consumes information.

punchline.text: Real names built real power — and real problems.

quiz.question: What feature made Facebook different from MySpace?
